1910: Back then, most things were bought at a general store or by catalog.
1920: Electric gadgets were brand new in many homes.
1930: Money was tight, and most things were repaired, not replaced.
1940: Factories were busy, and many goods were rationed early in the decade.
1950: New suburbs filled with new appliances.
1960: Color, chrome and space-age styling were in every store.
1970: Prices rose fast, and wood paneling was everywhere.
1980: Malls were the place to shop, and gadgets went portable.
1990: Big-box stores grew, and computers came home.
2000: Online shopping started to change how people bought things.
2010: Phones replaced a drawer full of gadgets.
2020: Retro things became fashionable all over again.
